data_fields.name: item_chance_or_weight
data_fields.donor_constant: drop_rate; 10,000,000 = 100 percent; values of 1 or less become 10,000,000

data_fields.name: always_drop
data_fields.donor_constant: boolean; guaranteed in the independent list

data_fields.name: group_chance
data_fields.donor_constant: loot_groups.drop_rate; group chance = value / 10,000,000 x luck

data_fields.name: min_amount
data_fields.donor_constant: inclusive lower bound of the amount roll

data_fields.name: max_amount
data_fields.donor_constant: inclusive upper bound of the amount roll

data_fields.name: grade_distribution_weights
data_fields.donor_constant: 12 weights (Weight0 to Weight11) summing to a roll over 0-99

best_idea: A loot pack is a list of guaranteed or independently rolled items plus groups that each roll once and yield at most one item by weight, so a drop table reads as data with no script.
decision_why: Take the group-then-one-pick shape and the data-driven chances; reject the luck multiplier on the pick (it biases the pick, as read) and the ownership roll winner rule (reads as wrong).
acceptance: Server test: a pack with one guaranteed item and one 50 percent group of two entries weighted 3:1 gives the guaranteed item on every kill over 10,000 kills, the group drops about half the time, and when it drops the entries split about 3:1 (within 2 points) at luck 1.0 and at luck 1.5.
